cheek 0.2.3 improves download retries, fragment scheduling and transfer tuning.

- Interrupted HTTP ranges continue from the received prefix instead of downloading it again. Range responses are validated before writing.
- Retries respect Retry-After seconds and dates, add jitter, and reduce adaptive parallelism after failures.
- Adaptive transfers start with up to two requests and test higher counts against measured throughput. `-N` caps parallelism; `--fixed-connections` retains a fixed count and `--power-save` caps it at two.
- HLS and DASH fragments can finish out of order into temporary disk files and are assembled in order. A slow early segment no longer blocks later requests behind the scheduling window.
- `--http-protocol auto` permits HTTP/2 negotiation for comparisons; HTTP/1.1 remains the default.
- Compatible cover images convert during the final FFmpeg audio/mux/tag operation instead of a separate conversion step.
- A repeatable benchmark checks byte-exact output and records phase timings and optional sampled CPU/RAM usage. Short transfers may be slower with adaptive startup; general speed and Android energy gains have not been established.

Includes Linux, Windows, macOS and all three Android binaries used by Hamstr. Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
